name: Salpornithidae
description: Spotted Creepers are a small family of tree-creeping passerine birds found in Africa and Asia. Unlike true treecreepers, they have spotted and barred plumage and frequent open woodlands rather than dense forests.

children.name: Salpornis
children.description: A genus of bark-gleaning passerines with heavily spotted and barred plumage, found in Africa and India.

children.name: Salpornis spilonotus
children.description: The Indian spotted creeper (Salpornis spilonota) is a small passerine bird that is a member of the family Salpornithidae, which was previously treated as a subfamily of Certhiidae.

children.name: Salpornis salvadori
children.description:
The African spotted creeper (Salpornis salvadori) is a small passerine bird in the family Salpornithidae. It is found in subsaharan Africa in open deciduous forest and mango groves. It does not migrate other than local movements.
The African spotted creeper has strongly spotted and barred plumage, closely similar to the Indian spotted creeper, but clearly different from the treecreepers in the genus Certhia. It weighs up, twice as much as treecreepers of similar length [up to ].
